name: MxD
old_description: MxD (Manufacturing x Digital), the nation’s Digital Manufacturing & Cybersecurity Institute, is a solution-neutral advisor and convener. In partnership with the U.S. Department of War, we work to strengthen the U.S. industrial base.
about:
MxD operates from Chicago, Illinois, where it was founded in 2014 as the Digital Manufacturing and Design Innovation Institute (DMDII). It is the second of 18 institutes in the Manufacturing USA network, a national initiative to secure the future of U.S. manufacturing through innovation, collaboration, and education. The institute was established in partnership with the U.S. Department of War, which remains a founding member and co-investor in its research and demonstration portfolio.

The institute does not produce parts but runs a 22,000-square-foot Factory Floor that demonstrates digital manufacturing technologies, cybersecurity solutions, and training spaces for the current and future workforce. Members such as Siemens, EY, DMG MORI, and Betacom use the floor for experimentation with AI, robotics, AR/VR, digital twins, and 5G. MxD's three pillars — convene, advance, empower — guide its work: convening manufacturers, academia, and government; advancing digital adoption and secure cybersecurity practices; and empowering the workforce through accessible learning tools. More than 350,000 learners have engaged with MxD Learn programs, and the Virtual Training Center offers online courses from AI to cybersecurity.

MxD serves the U.S. industrial base with a focus on defense collaboration. As the Department of War-designated National Center for Cybersecurity in Manufacturing, it develops programs to protect supply chains from cyber attacks, including a Cyber Resource Hub and CMMC compliance guidance. The institute works closely with the Organic Industrial Base — government-owned facilities that produce munitions and maintain weapon systems — to modernize Army and Marine Corps industrial operations. Its network of over 350 members spans industry, academia, and government.

MxD was created to transform the outdated image of manufacturing into a clean, safe, and visionary technology leader, improving productivity, quality, and global competitiveness. Its mission is to strengthen U.S. manufacturing competitiveness through technology innovation, workforce development, and cybersecurity preparedness, ensuring a reliable industrial backstop in times of war and emergency.

name: NU Packaging
old_description: Jim founded NU Packaging in 2001 after spending two decades in the industry, driven by a desire to bring a greater sense of fun and creativity to packaging. Over the past 25 years he poured his passion, deep knowledge, and genuine warmth into building a company that values innovation, reliability, and a welcoming, friendly spirit, making NU Packaging a trusted partner for countless clients. Though we were deeply saddened by Jim’s passing in June 2025, his vision and enthusiasm continue to inspire and guide our team every day as we honor his legacy by carrying forward the culture, values, and commitment he created.
about:
NU Packaging operates from Salt Lake City, Utah. The company was founded in 2001 by Jim, who had spent two decades in the packaging industry and wanted to bring a more creative, enjoyable approach to the business. It remains family-owned and operated. Jim passed away in June 2025, and the team continues to run the business according to his original vision.

NU Packaging functions as both a wholesale packaging distributor and a box manufacturer. Following the acquisition of a local box-making facility, the company produces custom-sized corrugated boxes on demand at its Salt Lake City plant. It also provides vendor-managed inventory (VMI) and stocking agreements backed by live inventory reporting updated every 12 hours. Delivery runs daily with next-day service to the Salt Lake and Utah Valleys, and twice weekly to Davis and Weber Counties with on-demand flexibility. The staff collectively holds over 120 years of packaging experience.

The company serves businesses across the Wasatch Front, from startups to large regional retailers. Its customer base includes technology firms in the Silicon Slopes corridor, manufacturers in Ogden and Davis County, and other organizations needing wholesale packaging supplies, custom corrugated designs, or automated packaging solutions.

Jim started the company to inject a sense of fun and creativity into packaging, emphasizing innovation, reliability, and a welcoming culture. NU Packaging differentiates itself through a local, human-staffed customer service team, on-demand manufacturing that cuts material waste and shipping costs, and a "Full Package" model that designs, manufactures, stocks, and delivers packaging under one roof.

name: National Bushing & Parts Co
old_description: Since 1920, National Bushing & Parts Company has served professional installers and serious do-it-yourself customers throughout Minnesota with quality parts, supplies and service. During the 1990s, the National Bushing name transitioned to the Auto Value banner. Today, there are more than 160 company stores and independent store customers throughout Minnesota, North Dakota, Wisconsin and Michigan.
about:
National Bushing & Parts Co. traces its roots to 1920 when Ray Riley and Aime Pouliot founded the company in Minneapolis, Minnesota. The pair began by manufacturing bronze bushings and distributing replacement parts for early automobiles such as Pierce Arrow, Packard, and Ford, as well as truck, bus, and tractor components. In the 1990s the National Bushing name transitioned to the Auto Value banner, and the business is now headquartered in Mora, Minnesota, under the ownership of the Bartlett family, which has led the company for three generations.

Today the company operates as Automotive Parts Headquarters (APH), a wholesale distributor serving a network of more than 160 company stores and independent store customers across Minnesota, North Dakota, Wisconsin, and Michigan. A 160,000-square-foot distribution center in St. Cloud, opened in 2006, supports warehousing and logistics for the Auto Value brand. APH has been a member of the Aftermarket Auto Parts Alliance since 1986, leveraging the coalition’s purchasing power and branding.

The customer base includes professional installers and serious do-it-yourself buyers seeking automotive aftermarket parts, supplies, and service. Historically the catalog covered components for passenger cars, trucks, buses, and tractors; the current offering spans the full range of aftermarket repair parts sold through the Auto Value retail network.

The company’s early reputation for machine-shop expertise and a diverse inventory helped it become one of the upper Midwest’s parts wholesalers. Leadership emphasizes carefully designed growth strategies and the strength of the Alliance affiliation, which the Bartlett family credits for sustaining expansion well into the future.

name: National Content & Technology Cooperative
old_description: Since 1984, the dream of being more competitive, smarter and more efficient in building and maintaining a coax and fiber plant has compelled us all to do more. Whether that’s launching new services, managing customer expectations or elevating our offerings,
about:
National Content & Technology Cooperative (NCTC) is a not-for-profit cooperative headquartered in Overland Park, Kansas. Founded in 1984, the organization began with the goal of helping independent broadband and pay-TV providers become more competitive, smarter, and more efficient in building and maintaining coax and fiber networks. Its founding mission was to help members competitively acquire video programming and vital technologies needed to offer services that define their communities’ infrastructure.

NCTC does not manufacture physical products; instead, it aggregates buying power and provides services across content, connectivity, video, and procurement. The cooperative negotiates programming and streaming agreements with more than 200 TV networks on behalf of its 700-plus member companies, which collectively serve roughly one-third of all households and businesses in North America and U.S. territories. Its connectivity portfolio includes IP transit and transport, DDoS mitigation, analytics, SD-WAN, DNS, cloud, and CDN services. NCTC also offers video platform solutions and operates a group-purchasing marketplace that gives members a single point of contact for technology procurement, contract management, and supplier performance.

The cooperative’s members are independent communications service providers—broadband and pay-TV operators—ranging from small rural operators to larger regional players. Network providers and suppliers such as CommScope, eero, TiVo, Cogent Communications, Lumen, and Zayo Group work through NCTC as a gateway to reach this diverse member base. NCTC’s supplier directory lists dozens of approved and preferred partners across hardware, software, and professional services.

NCTC’s differentiating premise is that collective purchasing power enables members to secure deals they could not obtain individually. The cooperative emphasizes a streamlined, one-stop procurement process, defined service-level commitments, and ongoing technology innovation to help members remain profitable and sustainable in a rapidly changing industry.

The company emphasizes its 50-year legacy, personalized service, and a limited lifetime warranty on products. It positions itself as a partner in creating homes that reflect the customer's style, combining craftsmanship with customization.

name: Nesson Cable Engineering
old_description: Founded in 1981, Nesson Cable has been building, upgrading, and maintaining telecom systems for over 40 years. Experts in both the technical and construction aspects of the industry, we offer a turnkey product to our customers
about:
Founded in 1981 in Fruitport, Michigan, Nesson Cable Engineering (NCE) has spent over four decades building, upgrading, and maintaining telecommunications systems across the Lower Peninsula.

NCE handles both coaxial and fiber-optic networks, providing directional drilling, aerial and underground construction, splicing, and technical activation. The firm uses qualified subcontractors for conduit placement and cable pulling but keeps all splicing and technical work in-house, performed by employees who average 15 years of experience. This model extends to emergency restoration, NJUNS coordination, plant relocations, and ongoing system maintenance.

The contractor serves telecommunications providers, municipal governments, road commissions, and the Michigan Department of Transportation (MDOT). Projects routinely involve coordination with cities, businesses, and residents, including traffic control, hard-surface potholing, and remediation of incidental damage to lawns, sidewalks, and sprinkler systems.

NCE was founded on the premise that competence comes from retaining experienced staff and making them the last to touch every project. The company emphasizes accountability, permanence, and problem prevention through pre-construction surveying that identifies clearance issues, avoids make-ready costs, and reduces pole denials before they arise.

name: NetVia Group, an Epec Company
old_description: NetVia Group is a manufacturer of high-reliability, advanced printed circuit board technology. For more than 35 years, the most advanced and innovative technology companies have relied on NetVia Group for all their time-critical, high-performance PCB solutions. We specialize in multi-layer PCBs, rigid circuit boards, flexible circuits, and rigid-flex printed circuit boards that meet IPC-6012/6013/6018 Class 2, Class 3, and Class 3/A qualifications.
about:
NetVia Group operates from Irving, Texas. Founded more than 35 years ago, the company became part of Epec Engineered Technologies in 2019, continuing a legacy of high-reliability printed circuit board manufacturing.

The company produces multi-layer rigid, flexible, and rigid-flex printed circuit boards, including high-density interconnect (HDI), RF/microwave, and hybrid designs. Its facility houses equipment such as 300,000 RPM mechanical drills, UV laser drills, laser direct imaging, reverse pulse plating, automated planarization, and a range of inspection systems including AOI, X-ray, and flying probe testers. The shop focuses on quick-turn, high-technology boards meeting IPC Class 2, 3, and 3/A standards.

Customers span defense and aerospace, telecommunications, commercial high-density interconnect, oil and gas, scientific, and medical sectors. The company highlights its ITAR registration and long history supplying military and defense programs, as well as providing PCBs for microwave phased-array antenna tiles and beamforming subassemblies.

NetVia Group emphasizes its heavy reinvestment in equipment and engineering to handle complex designs that other suppliers decline, and it targets turnaround times without compromising quality.

name: Never Stop Building LLC
old_description: Never Stop Building is a design-build studio located in central Maine. We specialize in traditional woodworking, furniture design, timber framing, tokonoma, shoji doors, and gates, utilizing predominantly Japanese tools and techniques.
about:
Never Stop Building LLC operates as a design-build studio in Mercer, Maine, a small town in the central part of the state. The company was founded in 2013 by Jason Fox, who initially launched the venture as an engineering and prototyping business. A lifelong interest in Japanese history and culture, combined with a background in machining and computer-aided design, eventually steered the firm toward the precise world of Japanese woodworking.

The studio specializes in traditional woodworking, furniture design, timber framing, and finish carpentry, producing items such as tokonoma alcoves, shoji doors, gates, and custom furniture pieces. Work is carried out using predominantly Japanese hand tools and techniques, and the shop also passes on those methods through woodworking classes and timber-frame workshops often led by guest masters. Project examples include a yellow cedar partition wall, a fir slab dining island, a walnut entry door, and a hexagonal hot tub.

The client base spans residential homeowners, hospitality operators, and commercial spaces seeking custom woodwork. Past projects range from a garden shed and a mountain home to a Kyoto-inspired tea room, a sushi counter, and a sauna, indicating a focus on high-quality, bespoke installations for both private and public environments.

Fox describes the company's guiding principle as a covenant to "honor the tree," sourcing lumber directly when possible and favoring natural finishes. The design philosophy blends Japanese aesthetics with Shaker and Mid-Century Modern influences, aiming for what he calls "utilitarian elegance" — simple, clean forms that let the material speak for itself.
